written.text: Write a Precis of the given passage, condensing it to approximately one third of the original length and give a title for the same.(15) Morality constitutes the invisible framework that upholds the ethical foundation of any society, governing the conduct of individuals and shaping the collective conscience of a civilization. It transcends mere legality or convention, embodying the intrinsic sense of right and wrong that determines the moral tenor of human interactions. A society’s moral fabric is neither static nor universal; it evolves in response to cultural, religious, and philosophical influences, reflecting the values and principles its people deem essential for harmonious coexistence. Without a moral compass to guide human behaviour, even the most sophisticated social structures risk descending into chaos and ethical decay. The vitality of morality lies in its capacity to generate mutual trust and social cohesion. Moral principles such as honesty, compassion, integrity, and justice serve as the cornerstones of cooperative living, enabling individuals to interact with respect and empathy. When citizens adhere to shared ethical norms, society achieves a sense of unity and purpose greater than the sum of its parts. Conversely, when morality erodes under the pressure of materialism, corruption, or moral relativism, social divisions deepen, and institutions lose their legitimacy. In this sense, morality functions as both the glue and the safeguard of civilization. Throughout history, moral thought has been shaped by various philosophical traditions and religious doctrines. From the Aristotelian notion of virtue ethics to Kant’s categorical imperative and the utilitarian emphasis on the greatest good for the greatest number, thinkers have sought to define the basis of moral responsibility. These philosophical foundations continue to influence modern ethical discourse, guiding laws, education, and interpersonal relations. Despite cultural diversity, the universal aspiration toward moral goodness underscores humanity’s innate desire for justice and compassion, attesting to the moral continuity that binds civilizations across time and geography. In contemporary society, advances in technology, globalization, and social media have posed new moral dilemmas that challenge traditional ethical frameworks. Issues such as data privacy, artificial intelligence, climate responsibility, and social inequality demand a reevaluation of moral standards in light of modern complexity. The pace of change often outstrips the development of moral consensus, leaving individuals and institutions grappling with ambiguous ethical choices. As a result, the need for moral reflection and education becomes ever more urgent, not merely as a social requirement but as a condition for the preservation of human dignity in an increasingly impersonal world. Ultimately, morality serves as the spiritual and ethical compass of society, directing collective progress toward justice and human flourishing. It reminds individuals that true advancement lies not only in material prosperity but in the cultivation of virtue and the pursuit of truth. A morally grounded society fosters empathy over exploitation, fairness over greed, and altruism over selfish ambition. When guided by moral integrity, civilization ascends beyond mere survival to achieve a higher form of human excellence—one in which wisdom, virtue, and conscience define the essence of progress.

Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow: Economic inequality, a condition deeply entrenched in many modern societies, has become a pressing concern for both policymakers and scholars. This imbalance, evident in the unequal allocation of wealth and resources, frequently intensifies social divisions and poses substantial obstacles to fair access to opportunities. Such widespread disparity undermines the core pillars of social unity, making the goal of shared prosperity ever more difficult to achieve. Over time, a multitude of factors have driven economic inequality, ranging from colonial exploitation and uneven globalization to unpredictable fiscal policies. These historical influences have combined to create entrenched socioeconomic structures in which the affluent elite hold excessive sway over political and economic decisions. As a consequence, marginalized populations are often consigned to living in subsistence conditions, deprived of vital infrastructural resources. In contemporary contexts, technological advancement and capital markets have paradoxically fostered both unprecedented growth and deepening inequality. The ascendancy of automation, though ostensibly designed to enhance efficiency, has often displaced swathes of the labour force, thereby aggravating unemployment rates. At the same time, the expansion of speculative investment opportunities has further benefited individuals with existing wealth, deepening the divide between the rich and the poor. One cannot overlook the insidious ramifications of economic inequality on democratic institutions. When affluence confers outsized political leverage, public policy risks becoming skewed towards the preservation of privilege rather than the redress of injustice. This distortion undermines the legitimacy of governance, fostering cynicism amongst the disenfranchised and imperiling societal stability. Addressing economic inequality necessitates a multifaceted approach encompassing progressive taxation, expansive educational access, and robust social welfare mechanisms. Reforms must transcend mere palliative measures, aspiring instead towards the dismantlement of entrenched inequities. Only through such deliberate and comprehensive intervention may societies envisage a future wherein prosperity is both shared and sustainable.
